dedupe_keys.name: itu r p 832 world atlas of ground conductivities

description: Recommendation ITU-R P.832, the World Atlas of Ground Conductivities, gives maps of the electrical conductivity of the ground across the world, in millisiemens per metre, for use in predicting ground-wave propagation at low and medium frequencies. Ground conductivity controls how far long-wave and medium-wave (AM) broadcast signals, navigation aids and very low frequency systems travel along the Earth's surface, so the atlas underpins international planning of LF and MF broadcasting and the coordination of AM stations. The current edition, P.832-4, was approved on 22 July 2015 and is in force; it contains VLF maps (up to about 30 kHz) and MF maps standardised to 1 MHz, with earlier editions of the atlas dating back to 1993. Coverage: global land and sea, by region. Format and access: the Recommendation as PDF (English about 5.8 MB) and Word, with Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian and Spanish versions, free from the ITU website. Caveats: the maps are printed images, not gridded data, so users must digitise them; values are generalised and some regions rely on old submissions. Simulation uses: ground-wave coverage modelling of AM and LF broadcast and navigation transmitters, which matters for emergency broadcasting when other networks fail, and inputs for low-frequency propagation models. Related records: the NTIA LFMF propagation model takes ground conductivity as an input, the ITU BR IFIC holds the broadcast assignments, and the ITU-R propagation databanks hold measurement data.
